requirements.evidence: Both routes and the navbar links exist (routes/web.php:59-60, layouts/default-page.blade.php:49-55), every contract lang key is present in both locales (lang/en/ui.php:24-47, lang/pt_BR/ui.php:24-47), and all required properties/methods are implemented (app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php:22-207, app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php:32-88). Deviations: rename passes the raw draft name as the slug instead of a derived slug (Queues.php:130), the toggle is always labelled 'Deactivate' even for inactive queues (queues.blade.php:84), and the queues empty state reuses the members text (queues.blade.php:26).

conventions.evidence: Domain writes correctly go through actions (Queues.php:66,130,168,194,204; Serve.php:74), but $this->validate() is never called although #[Validate] is declared (Queues.php:25,61-66,121-130) and renameName has no validation attribute at all (Queues.php:36); several public actions skip $this->authorize (Queues.php:81,105,146,173); the callableQueues helper is public (Serve.php:50); no CHANGELOG/docs update and no tests are included.

security.evidence: Entity IDs are resolved with scoped queries (Queues.php:83,107,125,164,175,189,199; Serve.php:65) and writes authorize via QueuePolicy/actions (Queues.php:44,63,127,166,192,202; Serve.php:74), with #[Locked] on entity and lastCalledTicketId (Queues.php:22, Serve.php:32-33); however mode is client-writable and unvalidated, so CallMode::from($this->mode) can throw an uncaught ValueError (Serve.php:30,74), and openQueue/startRename/openAccess/confirmToggle never authorize the resolved queue.

tests.evidence: change.diff contains no tests/** files; it only adds app/Livewire/Entity/Queues.php, app/Livewire/Entity/Serve.php, two Blade views, routes and lang entries, so there are no happy-path, unauthorized-call or tamper tests for any new action.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses CreateQueue/UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess/CallNextTicket and adds no service/repository layer (Queues.php:66-232, Serve.php:74); minor duplication: the member/queue row markup is copy-pasted across queues.blade.php:14-24,143-149 and members.blade.php instead of a Blade component.

readability.evidence: Methods are small and names match sibling components (Queues.php:61-107, Serve.php:57-88), but the hidden fallback $id = $this->editingQueueId ?? $this->viewingQueueId (Queues.php:123) is subtle and __('ui.queues_active', ['default' => 'Active']) (queues.blade.php:21) passes a meaningless replacement.

scope.evidence: The diff only adds the queues/serve components and views, their routes, lang keys, navbar links and the members tabs; no unrelated refactors or features.

issues.explanation: No Pest/PHPUnit tests were added for either component, violating the mandatory test-first convention and leaving every new public action without happy-path, unauthorized-call or tamper coverage.
rename() passes slug: $this->renameName (the raw draft) instead of the slug re-derived from the name, so a rename to 'New Name' sends 'New Name' as the slug rather than 'new-name'.

create() and rename() never call $this->validate(), and renameName has no #[Validate] rule, departing from the project's #[Validate] + validate() pattern and leaving client input unvalidated by the component.
openQueue, startRename, openAccess and confirmToggle resolve queues but never call $this->authorize(...), despite the rule that every public Livewire action authorizes server-side.
mode is client-writable and unvalidated, so a tampered value makes CallMode::from($mode) throw an uncaught ValueError (HTTP 500) instead of being rejected or limited to any/priority_only/normal_only.
The detail and confirmation modals always render 'Deactivate' (ui.queues_deactivate), including for inactive queues, where the task asks for a reactivate affordance.
The empty queues list reuses ui.members_empty, showing the members empty-state wording instead of a queue-specific message.
callableQueues() is only used internally by mount()/render() but is public, contrary to the convention of keeping non-endpoint helpers protected/private.
No CHANGELOG entry or documentation update accompanies the new user-facing queues/serve pages and members tabs, and the new public methods carry no PHPDoc.
The row markup is duplicated across the queues list, access modal and members page instead of being extracted into a Blade component as the conventions require.
__('ui.queues_active', ['default' => 'Active']) passes a 'default' replacement that Laravel ignores, which is misleading dead weight.

review.summary: The change adds the queues management component, the attendant serve panel, their routes, lang keys, navbar links and members-page tabs, and it generally follows the existing Livewire/action patterns. It cannot be approved because it ships with no tests at all, rename sends the raw name instead of a derived slug, and several public actions lack validation or authorization, including a client-writable mode that can trigger an uncaught ValueError.
